title: Small Bets, Big Impact Building GenBI at a Fortune 100 – Asaf Bord, Northwestern Mutual
talk_summary: Asaf Bord describes building a GenBI agent at Northwestern Mutual using a phased, six-week-sprint roadmap where each phase ships a standalone productizable component (metadata agent, RAG report-finder, SQL agent, BI agent) and each phase feeds the next. The core transferable ideas are incremental deliverables with kill-points, using existing verified assets (certified reports) as a trust anchor and as few-shot seeds for harder generation, and building evals from real SME questions.

takeaways.what_they_do: Break the project into six-week sprints, each ending in a tangible deliverable that can be productized or the project stopped, so leadership retains control and sunk-cost bias is avoided.
Instead of generating SQL from scratch, first retrieve an existing certified report/dashboard; only fall back to SQL generation if no report fits, and use the report's query as a few-shot seed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're not going to even try to build SQLs... let's just bring information that is already in the ecosystem that's already verified
takeaways.numbers: ~80% of BI team work was routing to existing reports; automated ~80% of that 20% capacity (~2 FTE of 10)

takeaways.what_they_do: Work directly with the people who do the task daily to collect real questions and real answers, forming the eval set, and keep them involved so they validate the system.
takeaways.evidence_quote: gave us a lot of real life examples of what people are actually asking in a corporate and what people have answered to them. So basically the eval

takeaways.what_they_do: Four narrow agents (metadata, RAG, SQL, BI) coordinated by an orchestrator that decides which to invoke per question, with conversation-level caching to avoid redoing work.
A/B tested LLM performance on a database with good metadata vs poor metadata to prove enrichment value quantitatively.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we show how much better an LLM performs when having the right metadata in place

takeaways.what_they_do: Release first to expert users who can detect errors and give useful feedback, then to less-expert users, deferring executives until accuracy is proven.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're first going to release it to actual BI experts... people that would be able to do it on their own and know what good looks like
